title: Define composite SLI and progressive-variant-degrade error budget policy for high-churn endpoints
creator: Maya Patel
description:
Purpose: establish a per-endpoint composite SLI that captures both tail-latency and request-quality (model correctness signal) for chat and generation routes, and codify an error-budget-driven progressive variant-degrade policy that gracefully sheds load and rebalances KV cache priority during multi-region failover or capacity pressure. This ticket defines the telemetry, decision thresholds, and operational runbook needed for safe rollout and automated enforcement.

Background: Current SLO work focuses largely on single-dimension latency or availability. High-churn conversational routes show correlated degradation in both quality (semantic correctness / hallucination rate) and tail latency under load; a single metric leads to brittle circuit-breakers. We need a composite SLI that: (1) weights P95 latency and a model-quality score derived from eval prompts / canned promptset pass-rate, (2) exposes clear error-budget burn signals for each endpoint and model variant, and (3) drives a progressive degradation policy (stepwise variant demotion, KV-cache rebalancing, regional reroute) rather than immediate hard shutoffs.

Goals:
- Define canonical composite SLI formula per endpoint type (chat, text-gen, embeddings).
- Specify SLI buckets and aggregation windows (1m, 5m, 1h) for real-time alarm vs retrospective burn analysis.
- Define error budget bands (green/amber/red) and automated actions per band.
- Design progressive-variant-degrade policy that demotes model variants (A->B->C) with preconditions and cooldowns.
- Tie KV-cache eviction priorities to endpoint SLI impact so high-value routes retain cache under memory pressure.
- Produce a rollback/runbook and smoke-test plan for a staged rollout to hosted and dedicated clusters.

Out-of-scope: long-term cross-tenant pricing changes, private deployment install docs (these will follow in separate tickets).
acceptance_criteria: Composite SLI spec doc created and reviewed (chat/text-gen/embedding templates)
Alerting thresholds defined and implemented in metrics dashboard (1m and 5m realtime views)
Automated policy: progressive variant demotion implemented in orchestrator with safe rollback flags
KV-cache priority mapping implemented for top 50 high-churn endpoints and validated in canary
Runbook describing manual override, governance for cross-region borrow and return of error budget completed
End-to-end smoke test and postmortem checklist added to the ticket
updates: 2025-02-16: Kickoff meeting with SRE, Runtime, and Product. Agreed composite SLI should be expressed as weighted sum: 0.6*latency_score + 0.4*quality_score (initial weights subject to calibration). Action: Runtime to instrument latency_score buckets, Applied ML to produce baseline quality_score signals from nightly evals.

2025-02-18: Prototype quality_score pipeline landed in metrics ingestion (PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/telemetry/pull/914). Initial quality_score uses promptset pass-rate and a simple null-response detector. Note: current signal is noisy for low-traffic endpoints.
2025-02-20: Design review feedback (PM and SRE): require short-term fallback to latency-only gating for endpoints with quality signal sample < 1000 requests/day. Added as precondition to the policy.

2025-02-22: Orchestrator contract drafted: policy accepts inputs (endpoint_key, composite_sli_window, current_error_budget, kv_cache_hit_rate, regional_capacity_score) and outputs action (no-op, demote-variant, route-to-region, evict-cache-by-priority). Draft saved: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/RINF/ENG-65723+Composite+SLI+Spec

2025-02-24: Implemented canary for progressive-demote flow in staging clusters. Behavior: when composite SLI enters amber for 5m with rising burn rate, demote variant by one level and shift 20% traffic. Test scenario: injected latency + degraded quality using fault-injection harness. Observed graceful traffic shift and KV-cache rebalancing worked but caused cache churn on unrelated routes — follow-up: refine eviction policy to be endpoint-local where possible.

2025-02-26: SRE requested cooling window increased from 10m->30m between demotion steps to avoid oscillation. Updated policy accordingly and added exponential backoff for re-promotion. TODO: validate on multi-region failover simulation next week.

2025-02-28: Prepared runbook draft; added manual override flag and a one-click revert in Console for canaries. Open questions: cross-region error budget borrowing cap and billing implications — flagged for PM and Finance review (see comment thread).
checklist: Calibrate quality_score weights across 3 weeks of historical traffic
Implement threshold gating for low-signal endpoints
Add circuit-breaker health signals to tracing for easier RCA
Run multi-region failover simulation and capture metrics
Stakeholder review: Runtime, SRE, Product, Applied ML, Finance
Schedule canary in hosted region and Dedicated cluster
